title: LEXICAL-SEMANTIC CLASSIFICATION AND NAMING MOTIVATION OF TOPONYMS IN THE ANDIJAN REGION: A LINGUISTIC AND ONOMASTIC ANALYSIS
description: This study examines the lexical-semantic classification and naming motivation of toponyms in Uzbekistan’s Andijan region. Drawing on onomastic theory, semantic analysis, and source-critical methodology, it investigates ten selected geographical names, distinguishing synchronic semantic transparency from historical etymology and original naming motivation. The analysis identifies semantic domains associated with hydrological features, topography, settlements, agriculture, political titles, and evaluative meanings. It demonstrates that certain toponyms exhibit overlapping semantic characteristics, requiring a multidimensional classification approach. The study proposes an evidence-graded, multi-label annotation framework for systematic toponymic documentation. Its methodological contribution lies in distinguishing lexical interpretation from historically substantiated etymology, with implications for regional onomastic research and the accurate English-language representation of Uzbek geographical names.
